title: The role of thalamic deep brain stimulation in action adaptation
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate brain networks—that is, groups of interconnected nerve cells—that are involved in the control and adaptation of movement. To achieve this, we will record the electrical activity of nerve cells both at your deep brain stimulation (DBS) electrode and on the scalp during various movement tasks. In order to better understand the effects of deep brain stimulation on brain activity and motor control, all assessments will be conducted both with the stimulation turned on and with it turned off. Through this study, we aim to gain a deeper understanding of how the human brain controls and adapts movement.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient cohort: The primary diagnosis is either a tic disorder (F95.1, F95.2) or essential tremor (G25.0) according to ICD-10 criteria.
Treatment with deep brain stimulation (Percept PC or Percept RC neurostimulator).
Participant cohort: no additional inclusion criteria.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality
Severe psychiatric symptoms
Severe internal (medical) comorbidities
Severe neurological comorbidities or pre-existing conditions
Substance dependence (excluding nicotine)
Intellectual disability
